text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Italian artist GIOVANNI BATISTA TIEPOLO was born in 1696.
Australian cavalry commander SIR HENRY CHAUVEL was born in 1865.

American aviator WILBUR WRIGHT, who, with his younger brother ORVILLE, invented the first powered aircraft, was born in 1867. In 1903 the brothers built a 12-horsepower plane, and completed the first powered flight near Kitty Hawk in North
Carolina. WILBUR flew 852 feet (260 metres) in 59 seconds, while ORVILLE flew 120 feet (36.6 metres) in 12 seconds.

English-born comedian SIR CHARLES (SPENCER) CHAPLIN, much loved for his portrayal of a tramp in baggy trousers and bowler hat, was born in 1889. Before 'talking' films, CHARLIE CHAPLIN was the best known and most popular film star of his day. He was married four times, and starred in many films including "The Rink" (1916), "The Kid" (1920), "The Great Dictator" (1940) and "Limelight" (1952). CHARLIE CHAPLIN died at his home in Switzerland on Christmas morning in 1977.
Australian singer (mezzo-soprano) FLORENCE AUSTRAL was born in 1894.

British comedian TERENCE ALAN "SPIKE" MILLIGAN was born in India in 1918. His family moved to London in 1933, and MILLIGAN met up with HARRY SECOMBE and PETER SELLERS in 1945/46, eventually developing "The Goon Show" after a performance in May 1951.
British actor PETER USTINOV was born in 1921. He won an Academy Award for "SPARTACUS" in 1960, and published his autobiography "DEAR ME" in 1983.

American composer HENRY MANCINI was born in 1924. British singer DUSTY SPRINGFIELD (MARY CATHERINE ISABEL BERNADETTE O'BRIEN) was born in 1939. From 1968 she had ten top ten hits in Britain, the most successful was " You Don't Have To Say You Love Me" (1966). She tried a comeback in 1978 with the 'Pet Shop Boys'. Recent hits have been "Nothing Has Been Proved"
(1989) and "In Private" (1989).

British singer, guitarist and songwriter GERRY RAFFERTY was born in 1947. In 1971 GERRY released his first solo album. It was unsuccessful. He had more success with the group 'Stealers Wheel'. Their major hit was "Stuck In The Middle With You" (1973). In 1978 he attempted a solo career again and released his "City To City" album. The hits included "Baker Street" and "Night Owl". In 1987 he produced the Scottish twins 'Proclaimers'.
Australian pop singer and cabaret artist COLLEEN HEWETT was born in 1950, in Bendigo, Victoria.
The youngest of the OSMOND brothers, JIMMY, was born in 1963. His hits included "Long-haired Lover From Liverpool" (1972) and "Tweedle Dee" (1973).
** EVENTS **
1746 : The Duke of Cumberland's forces defeated the
Jacobite Scots at the Battle of Culloden, near Inverness, Scotland.
1828 : Spanish painter FRANCISCO DE GOYA, whose deafness
changed the nature of his work often making it macabre and menacing, died.
1850 : The founder of the famous museum of waxworks in
London, MADAME MARIE TUSSAUD, died at the age of 89.
1879 : BERNADETTE SOUBIROUS (Saint BERNADETTE of Lourdes)
died. Her visions of the Virgin Mary led to the foundation of the shrine of Lourdes in France.
1883 : PAUL KRUGER became President of the South Africa
Republic.
1912 : Reports from many of the 691 people who survived

the sinking of the TITANIC suggested there weren't enough lifeboats to handle the 2,224 people on board the luxury liner when it hit an iceberg and sank in the North Atlantic. More lives would have been lost, had the liner "CARPATHIA" not reached the TITANIC within 80 minutes of its sinking.
1917 : VLADIMIR ILYICH LENIN returned to Russia with
German help, after 3 years of exile in Zurich.
1922 : The Soviet Union and Germany signed the Treaty of
Rapallo under which Germany recognised the Soviet Union as "a great power" and diplomatic and trade relations were restored.
1953 : The Royal Yacht 'Britannia' was launched.
1964 : Nine men received sentences of between 25 and 30
years for their part in Britain's 1963 "Great Train Robbery".
1964 : GERALDINE MOCK completed the first solo
round-the-world flight by a woman.
1969 : DESMOND DEKKER became the first Jamaican artist to
reach the top of the U.K Singles Charts, with "The Israelites".
1975 : The Communist KHMER ROUGE seized the capital of
Cambodia, Phnom Penh.
1988 : PLO military leader KHALIL AL-WAZIR, also known as
ABU JIHAD, was assassinated in Tunis.
1990 : Freed African National Congress leader NELSON

MANDELA publically thanked the world for its support during his 26 years of imprisonment by the South African Government. He did so during an appearance at a special concert in his honour at Wembley Stadium.
1992 : Italian financier CARLO de BENEDETTI and 32 others
were convicted of fraud in connection with the 1982 collapse of Banco Ambrosiano.
1995 : The European Union and Canada ended a bitter
dispute over fishing rights in the north Atlantic with a deal both sides said would protect threatened fish stocks.
1996 : An Italian court found disgraced former prime
minister BETTINO CRAXI guilty on further charges of corruption and sentenced him to eight years and three months in prison.
1996 : Queen ELIZABETH's second son Prince ANDREW and his
controversial wife SARAH, popularly known as Fergie, announced they were to divorce after 10 years of marriage.
